title: Short Stuff: Hollywood Sign
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Hollywood Sign, which turned 100 in 2023. Josh and Chuck cover its origin in 1923 as a billboard for the Hollywood Land real estate development, its deterioration and rebuilding by the Hollywood Chamber of Commerce, and the 1978 restoration fundraiser by Hugh Hefner at the Playboy Mansion, where letters were sponsored by celebrities such as Alice Cooper, Gene Autry and Andy Williams. They describe the 2010 threat to land next to the H (owned by Howard Hughes' estate) and Hefner again helping the city keep it. They discuss viewing spots, the sign's height, and the 1932 death of aspiring actress Peg Entwistle, who jumped from the H. The episode closes with a Betty Davis anecdote about Fountain Avenue.

segments.title: Opening and centennial
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the Hollywood Sign, celebrating its centennial in 2023, and note it was first built in 1923 as a billboard for Hollywood Land.

segments.title: Original Hollywood Land billboard
segments.summary: The original sign said Hollywood Land and advertised a real estate development. It cost about $21,000 to build, was built of plywood, and lasted well past its expected 18 months, into the 1940s. It was lit by about 4,000 light bulbs and was not lit at night.

segments.title: Chamber of Commerce rebuild
segments.summary: By the late 1940s the sign was in disrepair and the Hollywood Land company was gone. The Hollywood Chamber of Commerce stepped in to rebuild it as a sign reading Hollywood. It stayed in good shape for about three decades before deteriorating again in the 1970s.

segments.title: 1978 restoration by Hugh Hefner
segments.summary: Hugh Hefner raised money for the 1978 restoration of the sign with a party at the Playboy Mansion. Donors could sponsor a letter for $27,000. Alice Cooper sponsored the O in honor of Groucho Marx, and Gene Autry and Andy Williams also sponsored letters. The sign was torn down and rebuilt in steel rather than plywood and sheet metal.
topics: Alice Cooper Hollywood Sign letter sponsorship

segments.title: 2010 threat to land beside the H
segments.summary: In 2010 it emerged that land just left of the H, in Griffith Park, was privately owned, having been bought by Howard Hughes. A developer bought the parcel in 2002 for $1.67 million and offered it for $22 million eight years later. The city tried to raise the money and Hugh Hefner again stepped in to help.
topics: Howard Hughes land near Hollywood Sign

segments.title: Viewing the sign and the Casey Shriner guide
segments.summary: Casey Shriner's book Discovering Griffith Park describes fourteen good views of the sign. The trail ends behind the sign, which is not a good viewing spot. The sign is about fifty feet tall, and Chuck describes a good view from northbound Gower.

segments.title: Peg Entwistle's death in 1932
segments.summary: Aspiring actress Peg Entwistle, age 24, died in 1932 after jumping from the H of the sign. She had tried for a while to build a career, had a bit part in a film and appeared in plays, and is believed to have climbed to the top using a ladder a workman left behind. Betty Davis reportedly said she wanted to be like Peg Entwistle.

segments.title: Betty Davis and Fountain Avenue anecdote
segments.summary: Chuck recounts a reported Betty Davis remark that aspiring starlets should take Fountain Avenue to get into Hollywood, since it is a quicker east-west cut-through.

segments.title: Shout-outs
segments.summary: Josh gives shout-outs to listeners and friends, with a brief joke about a listener named Chuck Hippie Rob.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh says the episode is a Short Stuff installment. The hosts sign off with the show credit and the iHeartRadio app plug.
